questions: Does steering_oscillation on the oval fall back below about 0.2 from 0.272 with the 0.10 m track?
Does max_error move below 0.06 m, or does it stay near 0.062 to 0.063 m? If it stays there, is the reaction point (sensor y) now the limit?
Does oval progress hold near 0.44, or does it drop with the wider track?
Is there any sign of line loss at the outer sensors (x = ±0.06 m) on the slalom?

intent: Widen the track from 0.09 m to 0.10 m to bring steering oscillation back under about 0.2 on the oval, while keeping the sensing array and drivetrain that removed line loss and recovered oval progress in iteration 2. Expected: steering_oscillation near 0.2 or lower on the oval, progress around 0.4, line_loss_events at 0, and max_error possibly still near 0.062 m.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that narrowing the track gained progress (oval 0.31 to 0.44) but raised oscillation past the threshold (0.173 to 0.272), so the track width sets the yaw-gain-to-oscillation trade. Iteration 3 tests whether 0.10 m restores stable steering while keeping that progress. If max_error still stays at about 0.062 m, the next test is the sensor row at y = 0.02 m, and the controller's kp/kd would need retuning to match.
rationale: Iteration 2 (0.09 m track, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m body) raised oval progress from 0.31 to 0.44 and scored 111.9, the best so far. But max_error still sat at 0.063 m, so every run still left the track. Oval steering_oscillation jumped from 0.173 to 0.272, above the Integrator's 0.2 threshold, and slalom oscillation rose to 0.224. The narrow track is raising yaw gain per command, so the controller is overshooting. The Integrator's stated rule applies: widen wheel_track toward 0.10 m to reduce yaw gain per command. I am changing only wheel_track, from 0.09 to 0.10 m. Mass, body, wheel radius and the sensor array stay fixed so the result isolates the track change. Line loss stays at 0 with the seven-sensor, 16 mm array, so sensing is not the limit. Expected result: oval steering_oscillation falls back below about 0.2, slalom oscillation falls, and progress holds near 0.4. max_error may stay near 0.062 m, which would make the reaction point (sensor y) the next lever.
